fieldMarks: Long bushy tail ringed black and white, roughly as long as the head and body
Buffy body with dark brown wash and pale buff underparts
Black or dark brown eye rings set in buffy patches
Cat-like body, fox-like face, large oval ears, semi-retractable claws
behavior: Mainly nocturnal, also at dusk and dawn; active year round
Omnivorous but prefers animal matter: arthropods, small mammals, fruit, birds, reptiles, amphibians
Calls include an explosive bark and a piercing scream
Secretive; occurs singly or in pairs; changes dens often
habitat: Rocky areas with cliffs, crevices, canyons or talus in desert scrub, chaparral, oak and pinyon-juniper woodland and montane conifer forest, usually within 0.5 mile of water.
range: Western North America north to southern Oregon, northern Nevada, northern Utah, southern Wyoming and Colorado, south through California, Arizona, New Mexico and Texas into Mexico; old records from Kansas.

lookalikes.name: Raccoon
lookalikes.howToTell: ADW notes a ringed tail much like a raccoon's; ringtail is far slimmer, cat-like, with a much longer tail.
